entrypoints.summary: The sequencer RPC exposes citrea_sendRawDepositTransaction, whose handler dry-runs caller-provided deposit bytes and, on success, adds them to deposit_mempool.

affected_components.role: Independently dry-runs and queues deposit submissions.
Enforces one-time deposit processing by calculated txId.
Rejects a block path when a non-terminal system transaction is unsuccessful.

causal_paths.kind: same-state speculative admission to replay-protection failure

code_slices.fixed: No concrete patch code is present; the report states failed deposits are ignored during dry-running and excluded from blocks.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The executor returns EvmSystemTransactionNotSuccessful when an unsuccessful transaction is not the terminal system transaction.
code_slices.vulnerable: The RPC uses get_call to simulate a deposit and calls add_deposit_tx when the result is successful; Bridge.deposit requires processedTxIds[txId] to be false before setting it true.

negative_controls: A deposit that fails dry-running should not be included in a block under the reported resolution.
A non-duplicate deposit whose txId is not already processed does not trigger the cited replay-protection require.
observability.positive_marker: The executor emits the EvmSystemTransactionNotSuccessful error for an unsuccessful non-terminal system transaction; the audit describes the block as invalid and production as halted.

preconditions: The actor can invoke citrea_sendRawDepositTransaction; the audit says this was not available to regular users at the audited time but was intended to be opened later.
Two submissions of the same deposit are admitted before ordered system-transaction execution.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Two identical deposit byte payloads referring to the same calculated Bridge txId.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit the same deposit transaction twice in quick succession so both same-state dry-runs can be queued.

sources.concept: Duplicate submission of a replay-protected deposit through sequencer RPC

impact.affected_asset: Citrea block-production availability and block-validity processing.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a queued duplicate replay-protected deposit to fail during system-transaction execution, contingent on access to the deposit-submission RPC.
impact.security_effect: Block-production denial of service through invalidation of a block containing a duplicate system deposit.

causal_trace.summary: An actor able to invoke the deposit-submission RPC submits the same deposit twice in quick succession.

Each submission is independently simulated with get_call and admitted when that simulation succeeds, so duplicate deposits can be queued without preserving their joint executability against the replay-protection state that will advance during ordered execution.

The first executed Bridge deposit records its calculated txId as processed; the later duplicate fails the require that the same txId has not already been spent. The executor returns EvmSystemTransactionNotSuccessful for an unsuccessful non-terminal system transaction.
Because system transactions must succeed for block validity, the failed duplicate makes the block invalid; the audit reports this can effectively halt block production.

failure.operation: Bridge.deposit replay-protection require followed by executor rejection of an unsuccessful system transaction

primary_invariant.kind: admission-to-execution consistency for replay-protected system deposits
primary_invariant.statement: Deposits admitted into a candidate block must remain jointly executable in their execution order, including the one-time txId processing constraint enforced by Bridge.deposit.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Admission dry-runs each duplicate against the same latest-block state and queues both before the first execution mutates processedTxIds.

quality.review_notes: The report and audited source establish the described admission, replay-protection, and system-transaction failure path. No patch diff, regression test, or observed end-to-end execution result is in this bundle. The report states ordinary users could not access the RPC at audit time, so exploitability is conditional on RPC access.

remediation.invariant_restored: Failed deposits are ignored during dry-running and are not included in the block, preventing an unsuccessfully dry-run deposit from entering system-transaction execution.
mitigation_classes: admission/execution consistency for queued system transactions

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Submit the same deposit through the deposit RPC twice before execution advances state, contingent on being able to access that RPC.
data_structure_invariants: processedTxIds must not contain the calculated txId before Bridge.deposit marks it processed.
Queued system deposits must be jointly executable in their eventual order.
state_context.state_machine: A deposit moves from RPC dry-run admission to deposit mempool queueing to ordered system-transaction execution. The first execution consumes the txId; a queued duplicate then fails replay protection.

target.component: Sequencer deposit admission, EVM system-transaction executor, and Bridge deposit replay protection
